name: Sundance Documentary Fund
what: Grants for independent nonfiction feature films with contemporary relevance, from development through post-production.
amount: Development up to $40,000; production/post-production up to $100,000
eligibility: Independent nonfiction features with budgets under $1.2M; no shorts, series, fiction, advocacy or branded films; apply at least 8 months before picture lock; no fiscal sponsor required; international applicants accepted
next_window: Next call expected early 2027 (check site: the page also mentions 18 May 2026)
notes: Page gives conflicting timing: says next call opens 18 May 2026 and elsewhere 'to be announced in early 2027'. Shorts go to the separate Documentary Short Fund.

name: Catapult Film Fund Research and Development Grants
what: Early-stage grants for documentary films at the research and development stage, plus a Rough Cut Retreat run with True/False.
eligibility: Documentary projects in research or development; see guidelines on each opportunity page
next_window: Not yet announced; applications accepted in rounds
notes: Amounts not stated on the pages opened. Research Grant, Development Grant and Rough Cut Retreat all listed as closed for 2026.

name: Chicken & Egg Films Research & Development Grant
what: Grants for women and gender-expansive directors researching or developing a feature-length documentary.
amount: Research grants $10,000; development grants $20,000 ($450,000 total pool in 2026)
eligibility: Director identifies as a woman or gender-expansive; has completed at least one feature doc; feature-length (48+ min) independent nonfiction; based anywhere except countries under comprehensive US sanctions
next_window: Next cycle tentatively opens December 2026
notes: Organisation formerly Chicken & Egg Pictures; site now chickeneggfilms.org. Supported by Netflix.

name: IDA Pare Lorentz Documentary Fund
what: Finishing grants for independent feature documentaries in late post-production; the 2026 cycle theme is US influence.
amount: $25,000 per grantee (three grantees, one per round)
eligibility: Nomination by a partner organisation only; film budget up to $700,000; at least one director/producer has completed a nonfiction feature; no biographies, shorts, episodic, student or branded work; applicants can be based anywhere
next_window: Rolling rounds: Nov 2026, Feb 2027, May 2027 (nominations by partners; finalists apply early January for round one)
notes: Not an open call. 2026 first-round nominators: Brown Girls Doc Mafia, Catapult Film Fund, The Redford Center.

name: IDA Logan Elevate Grant
what: Grants for emerging women and non-binary filmmakers of colour directing feature-length journalistic documentaries.
eligibility: Emerging women or non-binary filmmakers of colour; feature-length journalistic documentary; nominated by partner organisations
next_window: Nomination-based; no dates stated
notes: Details taken from IDA's funding overview page; programme page itself not opened. Stage not stated - production assumed from journalistic feature focus, verify.

name: ITVS Open Call
what: Co-production funding for independent single nonfiction films in production or post-production, for public television.
amount: Up to $400,000 for features; up to $50,000 for stand-alone shorts (co-production agreement, not a grant)
eligibility: Single nonfiction projects 10-90 minutes in active production or post; no series, pilots or development-stage projects
next_window: Not yet announced

name: ITVS Incubator Fund
what: Early development money and a three- to six-month incubator for nonfiction features and web series aimed at public media streaming platforms.
amount: Up to $10,000, with potential additional funding up to $30,000
eligibility: Early-stage nonfiction features or web series for public media platforms
next_window: Not yet announced
notes: ITVS funding page lists no 'Diversity Development Fund'; this appears to be the current development route.

name: Field of Vision Submissions
what: Documentary unit that commissions shorts and supports feature and episodic films at development, production or post-production.
eligibility: Filmmakers of all experience levels; any length; does not acquire finished films
next_window: Rolling - no funding cycles or deadlines
notes: Amounts not stated. Separate forms for shorts, features/episodic and Field Notes.

name: Firelight Media Documentary Lab
what: Twelve-month fellowship with a project grant and mentorship for emerging filmmakers of colour on a first or second feature documentary.
eligibility: Emerging filmmakers of colour based in the US or US territories; director only; first or second feature doc; 2026 cycle accepted post-production only; no shorts, series or student films
next_window: Not yet announced

name: Firelight Media William Greaves Research & Development Fund
what: Unrestricted research and development grants for mid-career nonfiction filmmakers and artists of African and/or Indigenous descent in the Americas.
eligibility: Mid-career, of African and/or Indigenous descent, living and working in North, Central or South America or the Caribbean; nomination by an invited partner only
next_window: Not yet announced; 2026 nominations ran 1 May to 1 June
notes: Nomination-only via invited partners.

name: BPM Open Call
what: Production funding via licence agreement for nonfiction features about the Black experience; selected projects pitch at PitchBLACK.
amount: $20,000 production funding for up to five projects; one wins the PitchBLACK Award of up to $150,000
eligibility: Producer or director with 3+ years experience (or senior producer attached); at least one key team member a US citizen or green-card holder; feature-length (60+ min) nonfiction in pre-production, production or early post; no foreign-controlled projects
next_window: Not yet announced
notes: Funding is a licensing agreement, not a grant. Pitch at 10th PitchBLACK, June 2027.

name: CAAM Documentary Fund
what: Production and post-production funding for documentaries about Asian American experiences intended for public television.
eligibility: US citizens or legal residents 18+; applicant holds copyright and control; prior film/TV experience or sample; may need a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor; PBS-standard running times
next_window: Not stated on page

name: LPB Public Media Content Fund
what: Funding for programmes about Latino life and culture for public media.
eligibility: Application asks which team members are Latino/Latina and their roles; full criteria in guidelines and FAQ
notes: Pages opened did not state amounts, stages, eligibility rules or dates; stages assumed, verify against guidelines/FAQ pages.

name: Vision Maker Media Creative Shorts Fellowship
what: Funding, mentorship and training to produce a short film offering a fresh perspective on Indigenous experiences.
eligibility: Projects about Indigenous experiences with a community engagement plan; page does not state applicants must be Native
notes: Amounts and deadlines not stated on page; guidelines PDF not read. Vision Maker also runs a Native Youth Media Project.

name: PIC Media Fund
what: Funding for half-hour and one-hour nonfiction programmes about Pacific Islander stories, in production or post.
eligibility: Applicant holds copyright; nonfiction; must have completed a full-length documentary; production or post-production
next_window: Combined Media Fund / Shorts Fund calls open twice a year, spring and fall

name: PIC Shorts Fund
what: Funding for short films, short series or proof-of-concept shorts centred on Pacific Islander communities.
eligibility: Applicant holds copyright; Pacific Islander-focused training plan; key personnel and audiences reflect Pacific Islander communities; completion within 18 months
next_window: Combined Media Fund / Shorts Fund calls open twice a year, spring and fall

name: Perspective Fund
what: Funds impact-driven nonfiction films and documentary organisations via an inquiry form.
eligibility: Teams that build an impact-driven approach into the film; see FAQ
next_window: Inquiry forms; no deadlines stated
notes: Amounts and stages not stated; stages inferred from impact focus. 'Rolling' inferred from inquiry form with no deadline.

name: Gotham Week Project Market - Documentaries
what: Project market for in-development nonfiction work, with pre-scheduled one-on-one industry meetings during Gotham Week in New York.
eligibility: In-development documentary projects; see programme guidelines; fee $25 early / $45 final
next_window: Not yet announced; usual pattern is early deadline late April, final mid-May, market late September
notes: No cash award stated. Page labels timeline both 2025 and 2026, so exact dates not recorded. Email appears in page meta description.

name: SDF Production Grant
what: Production grants for nonfiction shorts, features, docuseries and experimental work made in or about the American South.
eligibility: Director lives in or has deep roots in AL, AR, FL, GA, KY, LA, MS, NC, SC, TN, VA or WV; 18+; US SSN or federal tax ID; no film students; production stage only
next_window: Not yet announced; check back for next annual cycle
notes: SDF also offers fiscal sponsorship.

name: NEH Media Projects: Development and Production Grants
what: Federal grants for humanities-based film, television, radio and digital media projects, for development or production.
amount: Development up to $75,000; production up to $700,000
eligibility: Organisations only (individual filmmakers typically apply via a nonprofit); see Notice of Funding Opportunity
next_window: Updated guidelines to be posted before next deadline
notes: Page header lists 5 May 2027 but also says the cycle deadline has passed; treat date as provisional. Development-specific page could not be opened (rate limit/client error).

name: NEA Grants for Arts Projects (Media Arts)
what: Federal project grants to nonprofit organisations, including media arts and film projects under the Visual & Media Arts discipline.
eligibility: US 501(c)(3) nonprofits, local government units or federally recognised tribes with 5+ years of arts programming; no individuals or fiscal sponsors
next_window: New guidelines expected by late December 2026; usual cycles February and July
notes: Two-part application (Grants.gov then NEA portal). Stages are indicative; NEA funds arts projects broadly.

name: NYSCA Electronic Media and Film
org: New York State Council on the Arts (NYSCA)
what: State arts funding for moving-image work including documentary; individual filmmakers apply under Support for Artists, organisations under Support for Organizations.
eligibility: New York State artists and organisations; see current Opportunity Guidelines
notes: Pages opened gave no amounts or deadlines; guidelines link labelled FY2025. Staff email obfuscated.

name: Jerome Foundation Film Production Grants
what: Production grants for early-career film directors based in New York City or Minnesota.
eligibility: Early-career directors (credits from 2017 onwards) resident in NYC or Minnesota; SSN or ITIN; two completed, publicly screened films; individuals only
next_window: Step 1 closed 1 Oct 2026; Step 2 is for invited applicants only
notes: Separate Submittable forms for NYC and Minnesota. Jerome also runs a MN Filmmaker Mentorship and the Jerome Hill Artist Fellowship.

name: Creative Capital Award
what: Unrestricted project funding and professional development for individual artists making new work, including film.
eligibility: Individual artists creating new work in disciplines including film
next_window: Not stated on page
notes: Open-call dates and residency rules not stated on pages opened; email obfuscated.

name: Guggenheim Fellowship (Film-Video)
what: Fellowships for mid-career professionals across more than 50 fields, including Film-Video.
eligibility: Citizens or permanent residents of the US or Canada; mid-career with notable contributions to their field
next_window: Not yet announced
notes: Amount not stated. Stages indicative - fellowships support the individual rather than a project stage.

name: Ford Foundation JustFilms
what: Grants for independent feature documentaries on social justice and inequality, through an open submission process.
eligibility: Feature documentaries of 50+ minutes with filmmaker creative control; not yet premiered; no shorts, series, impact campaigns, student, narrative or commissioned work
next_window: Not yet announced
notes: Amounts not stated. Weighted criteria: thematic alignment 30%, intersectional representation 25%, innovation 25%, viability 20%.

name: Kartemquin Diverse Voices in Docs (DVID)
what: Twelve-month cohort programme supporting emerging nonfiction filmmakers of colour in the Midwest.
eligibility: Emerging filmmakers who identify as Black, Indigenous or another person of colour, based in the Midwest
next_window: Not yet announced; 2026 window ran 1 Dec 2025 to 12 Jan 2026
notes: No cash amount stated; stages not stated on page and are indicative.

name: Points North Fellowship
what: Cohort programme for up to six feature documentary teams, with mentored workshops, a pitch at Camden International Film Festival and industry meetings.
eligibility: Early to mid-career nonfiction filmmakers worldwide; feature-length (60+ min) in production or post; fee $25-$45
next_window: Next cycle opens late 2026 to early 2027
notes: No cash award stated; covers flight, festival passes and accommodation.

name: SFFILM Documentary Film Fund
what: Post-production grants for feature-length documentaries.
eligibility: Feature docs (60+ min) in or near post-production; applicant 18+, ideally producer or director; open to filmmakers anywhere; no interview-led films or work for hire; application fee
next_window: Not yet announced

name: Austin Film Society Grant
what: Cash and in-kind grants for Texas-based filmmakers working in any genre, including nonfiction.
eligibility: Texas-based filmmakers
next_window: Feature films reopen spring 2027; short films reopen summer 2027
notes: Per-grant amounts not stated; has given over $3 million in cash grants to 570+ Texas filmmakers. Page does not name documentary explicitly.

name: JFI Grants
what: Completion funding for independent films that engage with Jewish history, life, culture or identity.
eligibility: Post-production with at least a strong rough cut; applicant 18+ with copyright and control; applicants need not be Jewish; no student or work-for-hire projects; application fee
next_window: Phase 1 final deadline 3 Dec 2026 (early deadline 6 Nov passed); Phase 2 by invitation, due 3 Mar 2027
notes: Amounts not stated on guidelines page. Not documentary-only.

name: Pulitzer Center Reporting Grants
what: Travel and reporting grants for journalists and filmmakers covering under-reported global stories, with a plan for US or European distribution.
eligibility: Staff or freelance journalists, writers, photographers, radio producers or filmmakers of any nationality; need credible plan for US and/or European media distribution
next_window: Rolling
notes: Grants page content appeared partly dated (references a 2017 pitch); reporting-grants subpage could not be opened. Verify current terms.
